claims.text: CrMnFeNi-based alloys are multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Replacing an EAM reference with an MLIP trained on diverse ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Neural-network or Gaussian-approximation potentials can serve as the proposed machine-learned reference potential.
The MLIP should be trained on a wide range of configurations sampled from ab initio molecular dynamics of the liquid.
The proposed method applies to complex multielement high-entropy alloys from approximately 0.8Tm to Tm.
The MLIP reference should cover both near-melting solid and liquid phases.
Training on comprehensive ab initio configurations will make the MLIP reproduce local atomic environments in the disordered liquid more accurately.
More accurate reproduction of liquid local environments will bridge the reference and target phase spaces.
An MLIP trained on diverse ab initio configurations will represent the configurational variety of the ab initio liquid better than an EAM potential.
Better representation of liquid configurations will reduce discontinuities and produce a smoother, lower-mismatch free-energy integration path.
The MLIP reference is predicted to reduce path mismatch by roughly 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
MLIP-based thermodynamic integration will produce free-energy differences closer to ab initio benchmark calculations.
TOR-TILD currently uses EAM reference potentials.
TOR-TILD's EAM potentials inadequately capture the multitude of configurations in an ab initio liquid and consequently cause larger TI path mismatches.
The method should be most effective for multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting because their configurational diversity is high.
The method may be less applicable to less-complex alloys or when reliable ab initio training data are unavailable.
Prior supporting evidence comes from elemental and binary calculations rather than complex multicomponent systems.
The proposed controlled benchmark compares EAM- and MLIP-reference thermodynamic integrations for the same representative alloy near melting against highly converged ab initio free energies.
The hypothesis is falsified if the MLIP gives less than a 20% statistically significant path-mismatch improvement or exceeds a predetermined free-energy error tolerance.
